rawFindings.title: Non-string map keys now overwrite properties in v1 object decoding
rawFindings.explanation: `readObject()` now assigns every decoded key into the target object, including object keys that are not valid property names. In Hessian maps, keys can be arbitrary values; this change turns distinct object keys into the same string key (`[object Object]`), so later entries overwrite earlier ones and previously skipped entries are no longer represented correctly.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the key-type guard, or convert non-string/number keys in a collision-safe way before assigning to a plain object.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Decoding a v1 map with two different object keys, e.g. `{ [new Date(1)]: 1, [new Date(2)]: 2 }`, now yields a single property `{"[object Object]": 2}` instead of preserving distinct entries.

rawFindings.title: v2 hash map decoding now stringifies unsupported keys into object collisions
rawFindings.explanation: `_readMap()` now writes every decoded key directly onto a plain object. Hessian maps can contain non-string keys, and plain-object assignment coerces them to strings, so different object keys collapse to the same property name and earlier entries are lost.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the plain-object assignment only for string/number keys, or store non-string keys in the existing `$map` representation instead of the object literal.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Decoding a v2 untyped hash map with two distinct object keys (for example two different `java.lang.Long` wrapper objects) now returns one property like `{"[object Object]": ...}` instead of two separate entries.
